Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Global Assurance Holdings Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Global Assurance Holdings Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Mark Herrera, Chief Claims Officer; and Jennifer Lee, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Global Assurance Holdings Inc.'s performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust net written premiums growth across our lines of business, improved expense ratio through operational efficiencies, positive premium growth guidance ahead, strategic capital deployment into high-return opportunities, solid investment income yields, healthy gross written premiums expansion, manageable catastrophe losses relative to our diversified book, and a prudent asset allocation that balances yield and risk. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Elena Vasquez, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong top-line growth in premiums, underwriting discipline, favorable investment returns, cost controls, reinsurance optimization, and strategic initiatives enhancing margins.

Let me start with our net written premiums, or NWP, which remains the cornerstone of our top-line growth. For the quarter, we delivered consolidated NWP growth of 11.2% year-over-year, reaching $4.8 billion. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing the industry average of around 7% as reported by AM Best for the P&C sector. On a constant currency basis, excluding the modest FX headwind from a stronger USD, growth was even stronger at 12.1%.

Breaking this down by line of business in our core segments—Personal Lines, Commercial Lines, and Specialty & Reinsurance—all figures net of cessions to our quota share and excess of loss reinsurance programs.

Personal Lines grew 9.8% year-over-year to $2.1 billion. This continues to be our growth engine, fueled by rate adequacy and strong retention amid a hardening market. Auto insurance led with 11.5% growth to $1.3 billion, driven by a 6.2% average rate increase—our third consecutive quarter of mid-single-digit hikes—supported by elevated repair costs from supply chain inflation and a 15% rise in used vehicle values per the Manheim Index. New business acquisition was robust at a book-to-bill ratio of 1.15x, bolstered by our telematics program, DriveSafe Insights, now active with 2.8 million policyholders. Usage-based insurance penetration hit 42%, up from 35% last year, delivering 20% better loss ratios through behavioral pricing algorithms powered by our partnership with Cambridge Mobile Telematics.

Homeowners grew 7.2% to $800 million, tempered by catastrophe exposure management. We achieved 4.8% earned rate increases, but selectively non-renewed 3% of our California book due to wildfire risk accumulation, aligning with our 1-in-250-year probabilistic catastrophe model. Retention held steady at 89%, above our 87% target, thanks to bundling initiatives with our homeowners-auto combo product, which now represents 65% of personal policies. Regionally, U.S. growth was 10.5%, while our UK personal motor book expanded 8% on the back of post-Brexit rate normalization.

Commercial Lines was the standout performer, up 13.4% year-over-year to $1.9 billion, reflecting our disciplined underwriting in a favorable pricing cycle. Middle-market property grew 15.2% to $850 million, capitalizing on 9-11% rate gains across the portfolio—our strongest in five years—amid reinsurance treaty renewals at January 1 that saw our ceded premiums rise only 2% despite cat bond issuances totaling $400 million for Florida and Gulf Coast wind exposure. Loss trends remain favorable, with severity moderated by our AI-driven peril modeling, which flagged a 12% reduction in modeled losses from Hurricane Idalia-like events.

Workers' Compensation surged 14.7% to $650 million, driven by payroll inflation normalization and a 7.5% rate uplift. Our book-to-bill here was 1.22x, with new business from large accounts in manufacturing and logistics, leveraging our CompSecure platform that integrates OSHA data for real-time risk selection. Retention improved to 92% from 89%, aided by dividend programs yielding 8-10% returns to policyholders. Regionally, North America contributed 75% of growth, but we're seeing early traction in APAC, where Australian workers' comp grew 18% on compulsory market reforms.

Small commercial, including our packaged BOP product, added 11% growth to $400 million, with enhanced distribution through independent agents via our digital quoting portal, which processed 250,000 submissions—a 40% year-over-year increase.

Specialty & Reinsurance delivered 8.6% growth to $800 million in a niche but volatile segment. Directors & Officers liability jumped 16% to $250 million, riding the wave of M&A resurgence—deal volumes up 25% per Refinitiv data—and cyber risk dislocation post-CrowdStrike outage analogs. We hiked rates 12% while expanding capacity through our Lloyd's syndicate, achieving a 1.30x book-to-bill. Cyber insurance grew 22% to $180 million, but we maintained strict attachment points above $50 million limits, with our CyberGuard Analytics tool—using machine learning on dark web signals—delivering a 25% edge in loss pick-up avoidance versus peers.

Our reinsurance assumed book, primarily property cat-XL from Bermuda platforms, grew 5% to $200 million, selectively layering above reinsurers like Swiss Re and RenaissanceRe at favorable terms. Retrocession ceded to third parties kept our net retention disciplined at 40%. Regionally, EMEA specialty was up 12%, driven by marine cargo amid Red Sea disruptions, while Latin America lagged at 4% due to Argentine currency volatility—we've hedged 70% exposure via NDFs.

Across the board, our NWP momentum stems from pricing discipline with an average earned rate of 7.1% per our actuarial models, volume expansion with new business up 18% year-over-year, and retention at 91% consolidated versus industry 88% per NAIC data. We've navigated headwinds like social inflation in liability lines—up 5% in indicated ultimate losses—and persistent auto repair inflation at 8.2% year-over-year per CCC Intelligent Solutions.

Technically, our Precision Underwrite platform, a cloud-based AI suite with Google Cloud integration, has optimized 75% of our U.S. commercial renewals, reducing cycle times by 40% and improving rate-on-rate accuracy to 95%. We're also piloting blockchain for parametric triggers in flood products, partnering with reinsurer Hannover Re.

Strategically, we view the current rate-hardening cycle—projected to peak mid-2025 per McKinsey—as a multi-year opportunity. We've allocated $500 million to capacity expansion via two tuck-in acquisitions: a cyber specialist in Singapore and a West Coast excess & surplus broker. Internationally, we're targeting 15% NWP growth in APAC by 2026 through joint ventures, like our recent tie-up with Ping An for personal lines in China. Looking forward, we expect Q4 consolidated NWP growth of 10-12%, with Personal Lines moderating to 8-10% on seasonal auto patterns, offset by Commercial acceleration to 14-16%.

Turning to gross written premiums, or GWP, which grew 8.7% year-over-year to $14.2 billion. This marks our ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit ex-cat growth, driven by disciplined pricing, strong retention, and targeted volume expansion. Excluding foreign exchange and prior-year development, organic GWP growth was 9.2%.

Personal Lines saw 11.4% GWP growth to $6.8 billion, fueled by a 7% average rate increase—our highest in five years—and policy count growth of 4.2%. Auto led at +13.2%, reflecting broad-based rate hikes of 9.5% to combat escalating loss costs from parts inflation up 15% year-over-year per CCC data and higher repair severities tied to supply chain disruptions. Retention held steady at 88.7%, bolstered by our AI-driven pricing engine incorporating real-time telematics from 65% of policies.

Homeowners grew 9.1% to $2.9 billion, driven by 6% rate actions amid catastrophe-heavy seasons. Wildfire exposure in California and Florida hurricane rebuilds pushed loss trends up 12%, prompting non-renewals of 15% of highest-risk coastal book while expanding in lower-hazard Midwest markets. U.S. growth was 12.1%, Europe added 8% via our AXA partnership in UK motor, and Asia-Pacific contributed 7% from bundled products in Singapore with parametric triggers.

Commercial P&C delivered 7.8% growth to $4.1 billion, balancing volume with selective underwriting. Workers' Compensation surged 10.2% to $1.6 billion on 5.5% rates and 3% policy count rise, with loss ratio improving 180 basis points to 92% via return-to-work programs and wearable tech cutting claim frequency 11% in construction. General Liability and Commercial Multi-Peril grew 6.5%, offset by middle-market gains. North America drove 8.2%, Latin America added 12% via Brazil fintech bundles.

Specialty Lines grew 14.6% to $2.1 billion, with Cyber up 22.3% to $850 million at 12% rates, maintaining ransomware exclusions for a 68% loss ratio. D&O grew 11.8%, Environmental Liability 16%. U.S./UK hit 16%, APAC 20%.

Life & Health grew 4.2% to $1.2 billion, with Term Life up 5.1% via digital portals, Health supplements 3%. Our VitalityAI app boosted persistency to 92%.

This GWP trajectory underscores profitable growth: 60% from rate and retention, 30% from tech-driven new business, 10% from M&A. We're allocating more to APAC for 15% CAGR.

Our combined ratio was 92.4%. On catastrophe losses, they came in at $475 million pre-tax for the quarter, or 14.2% of GWP, compared to $320 million or 10.1% last year. Year-to-date, $1.12 billion or 9.8% of YTD GWP. Dominated by Hurricane Idalia at $210 million, Midwest storms $145 million, California wildfires $120 million. P&C ex-cat loss ratio 58.2%, all-in 72.5%. U.S. property 68% of cats, Europe lighter at $45 million, Asia $35 million. Net retained $285 million after $190 million recoveries, 40% retention. PML capped at 8% of surplus. Pricing up 12.4% on U.S. property, cat modeling refresh with AIR Worldwide. Q4 cats expected 6-8% of GWP.

Now, expense ratio trends: Our consolidated expense ratio improved 130 basis points year-over-year to 27.2%, third straight quarter of improvement, nine-month trailing at 27.8% below our 28% target and industry 29.1% per AM Best. Contributed to best combined in five years ex-California fires.

Commissions and acquisition costs declined 8% to $1.82 billion or 9.9% of premiums from 11.2%, shifting to direct digital channels at 35% of new auto. Tied 60% commissions to retention/cross-sell. Operating expenses up 3% to $2.15 billion or 11.7%, flat sequentially on scale from $450 million premium growth, underlying up 1.2% ex-severance.

Tech Forward 2025: Guidewire Cloud automated 68% routine auto claims under $10k, cutting LAE 15%. ML models cut underwriting reviews 40%. AWS migration saved $28 million. ZBB identified $120 million savings, digital ads 3.2x ROAS. Digital expense ratio 18.5% vs. 32.1%.

U.S. 26.8%, Europe 12.4% post-Solvency II, APAC commissions high but direct model sub-20%. Guide full-year 27.5%, Q4 27.0%, long-term sub-26% by 2026 with gen AI.

Investment income for the quarter was $650 million, with book yield at 4.32% annualized on $145 billion portfolio, up 45 bps year-over-year and 12 bps sequentially—strongest since Q4 2007. 78% high-quality fixed income: 45% IG corporates, 20% Treasuries/agencies, 10% munis, 3% RMBS. Equities 8%, alternatives 14%. New money yield 5.15% vs. industry 4.7%.

Life/annuity 4.65% at 6.2-year duration, P&C 4.05% at 3.8 years. Reinvestments $8.2 billion at 5.4%, BBB industrials 6.2%, FRNs SOFR+145. U.S. munis 3.8%, Europe 3.2%, APAC 2.9%. ALM via Aladdin, credit upgrades, ESG 22% new, derisking to FRNs/T-bills. Q3 yield 4.45-4.55%.

We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with RBC ratio at 550%. On capital deployment, we hold $4.2 billion excess above 500% RBC U.S. and 180% Solvency II Europe. $2.8 billion deployable over 12-18 months targeting 14-16% ROE.

M&A 50% or $1.4 billion: Closed $450 million InsureTech Solutions for UBI, accretes 25 bps EPS. Eyeing $600-700 million cyber SME, $250 million Singapore microinsurance JV for APAC to $4 billion GWP by 2026. Europe opportunistic $300 million.

New products 30% $850 million: $200 million parametric AgriShield with IBM, $300 million Apex Embed API, $150 million green longevity annuities, $200 million AWS/Palantir underwriting. Repurchases $400 million, dividend up 10% to $1.02, 2.8% yield.

On asset allocation across $285 billion assets: Fixed income 72% $205.6 billion (gov/agency 28%, IG corporates 25%, securitized 12%, munis 7%), yield 4.8% Q2. Equities 15% $42.8 billion (public 12%, prefs 3%). Alternatives 13% $37.1 billion (private credit 5%, RE 4%, infra/PE 3%, hedge/cat bonds 1%). New money 5.9%, Sharpe 1.2. Targeting alts 15-18% by 2025.

Finally, premium growth guidance: Q4 2024 7-9%, FY 2025 8-10%. Personal 9-11%, Commercial 8-10%, L&H 5-7%. North America 9-11%, Europe 6-8%, APAC 12-15%. Rate 6.5% Q3, another 4-6% 2025, UBI 40%, embedded $500 million by '25 end.

Our expense ratio also improved to 27.2%.

David Patel: Thank you, Elena. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our Personal Lines, Commercial Lines, and Specialty segments. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophes and social inflation while implementing initiatives like Precision Underwrite and disciplined pricing strategies averaging 7.1% earned rates to improve risk selection.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in high-quality fixed income, private credit, and alternatives, with yields enhanced by ALM optimization and tactical shifts.

Mark Herrera: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI automation for 68% of routine claims and predictive analytics, resulting in reduced processing times, 15% lower loss adjustment expenses, and improved resolution rates.

Jennifer Lee: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new Guidewire Cloud platform and Tech Forward 2025 initiatives are expected to drive significant efficiencies, cost savings, and better underwriting accuracy.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on net written premiums growth by line?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, John. As Elena detailed, our 11.2% consolidated NWP growth to $4.8 billion was broad-based, with Commercial Lines at 13.4% leading due to middle-market property and workers' comp strength from 9-11% rates and 1.22x book-to-bill. Personal Lines at 9.8% on auto 11.5% with telematics driving UBI to 42%, and Specialty at 8.6% with cyber 22%. This positions us well for Q4 10-12% growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of catastrophe losses on your business?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Maria. Cats at $475 million or 14.2% of GWP were elevated from Idalia, storms, and wildfires, but net retained 40% at $285 million thanks to reinsurance. Ex-cat loss ratio pristine at 58.2%, combined 98.4% in corridor. We've priced accordingly with 12.4% property hikes and refreshed modeling for climate risks, budgeting Q4 6-8%.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like Solvency II reforms on your underwriting strategy?

David Patel: Thanks, David. Reforms provide tailwinds for streamlined compliance in Europe, trimming op-ex while maintaining discipline. We're enhancing cyber and parametric products with strict attachments, targeting attritional combined 92%, with APAC JVs like Ping An navigating local rules for 15% growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platform?

Jennifer Lee: Absolutely, Emily. Guidewire Cloud and Precision Underwrite automate 68% claims, cut underwriting cycle 40%, enable real-time telematics for 20% better loss ratios, and via AWS save $28 million. Digital expense to 18.5%, with gen AI targeting 80% claims automation by 2026, boosting NPS to 68 and cross-sell.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Hale with Credit Suisse. Please go ahead.

Robert Hale: Could you expand on expense ratio drivers and outlook?

Elena Vasquez: Sure, Robert. 27.2% improvement from 130 bps via digital shift curbing commissions to 9.9%, ZBB savings $120 million, and tech efficiencies. U.S. 26.8%, APAC improving with WeChat. FY 27.5%, Q4 27.0%, sub-26% long-term.

Operator: Our next question from Lisa Grant with Deutsche Bank.

Lisa Grant: Thoughts on capital deployment and FY25 premium guide?

Elena Vasquez: Lisa, $2.8 billion deployable: InsureTech closed, cyber and Singapore JVs advancing for APAC scale. Parametrics, embedded via Apex Embed, green annuities. Guide 8-10% FY25, Personal 9-11% on telematics, APAC 12-15%, backed by 92-94% combined.

Operator: [No more questions at this time.]

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Global Assurance Holdings Inc. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
